clue.text: A lot of bother with a stern old poet singer

indicators.note: a lot of a word, not all of it, so the synonym for bother loses its tail end

parts.note: bother means trouble
stern means dour, grim and severe

explanation.surface: A grim old poet who sings brings plenty of trouble with him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot of' trims TROUBLE to TROUB, dropping its last two letters LE.
explanation.definitionFit: Troubadours were medieval lyric poets of Provence who sang their verses of courtly love.

clue.text: Objection raised over a music producer

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the word is written upwards, bottom to top

parts.note: an objection is a 'but', as in 'no buts'

explanation.surface: Someone protests about a record producer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns BUT upwards to TUB, then A follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A brass instrument is something that produces music, here the deepest-voiced of the horns.

clue.text: There's no raising a riot out in this province

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising the word means writing it bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written before being turned

indicators.note: out as in disordered, so the letters of the words are shuffled

explanation.surface: In this province, nobody stirs up a riot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raising' turns NO into ON; 'out' rearranges A RIOT into TARIO.
explanation.definitionFit: A Canadian province whose capital is Toronto.

clue.text: Statement from these characters after match?

definitions.text: Statement from these characters after match?

parts.words: Statement from these characters after match?
parts.note: the characters are taken as the letters of a word for a weighing scale and a sheet of paper, and the financial statement is drawn up when accounts are matched

explanation.surface: Words spoken by the players once the game is over.
explanation.walkthrough: A cryptic definition: a company's accounts statement shows assets and liabilities matched against each other.
explanation.definitionFit: An accounting statement listing assets and liabilities on a set date, which must agree.

clue.text: Landed gentry abandon new attempt to change old levy

indicators.note: the gentry abandon some letters, which are taken out of the pool before the rest is shuffled
the remaining letters change their order, signalling a rearrangement

parts.note: an attempt is a try

explanation.surface: The landed gentry make another attempt to change an ancient tax.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove N and TRY from LANDEDGENTRY, leaving LADEDGEN, which 'to change' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A tax raised in Anglo-Saxon England to pay off Viking raiders.

clue.text: Posh knight goes to Irish county to relieve 9

parts.note: U is the old label for upper-class usage, so posh
N is the chess notation for knight
Cork is a county in the south of Ireland

explanation.surface: An upper-class knight travels to Ireland to give a narrow pass some relief.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 refers to the answer at 9 (BOTTLENECK); to relieve a bottle's neck is to pull the stopper.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulling the stopper frees the narrow top of a bottle.

clue.text: Champions of the Church, in Anglo-Saxon environment

indicators.note: an environment surrounds, so the Anglo-Saxon letters enclose the Church

parts.note: CE stands for Church of England

explanation.surface: Defenders of the faith in an Anglo-Saxon setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in ... environment' puts CE inside AS.
explanation.definitionFit: Experts or star performers are called aces, as are top fighter pilots.

clue.text: Illustrious warrior retired for a smoke

annotationWithheld.why: Illustrious warrior retired for a smoke: C(HERO)OT needs 'retired' to give COT (bed) and also to signal the insertion, one word doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Illustrious warrior retired for a smoke

clue.text: School department way off the main road?

parts.note: a side is a division of a school, such as the modern side or the classical side
a street is a way or road

explanation.surface: A school department that lies away from the main road.
explanation.walkthrough: Old British schools split teaching into 'sides', such as the classical side and the modern side.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor road branching from a thoroughfare lies away from the main route.

clue.text: It causes congestion, but we can stop it

definitions.meaning: a narrow point where traffic or work piles up
the narrow top of a bottle, which takes a stopper or cork

explanation.surface: Something blocks traffic, but we have the power to end it.
explanation.definitionFit: A traffic choke point and the stoppered top of a wine bottle share the name.

clue.text: Drink for an Aryan legislator, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word is pronounced, giving a sound-alike spelling

parts.note: a Mede, of the ancient people famous for the unalterable law of the Medes and Persians

explanation.surface: A beverage served to an ancient law-giver.
explanation.walkthrough: The Medes were an ancient Iranian people; 'the law of the Medes and Persians' cannot be changed.
explanation.definitionFit: Mead is an alcoholic beverage fermented from honey and water.

clue.text: As a form of punishment it had its ups and downs

definitions.text: As a form of punishment it had its ups and downs

parts.words: As a form of punishment it had its ups and downs
parts.note: the ups and downs are literal: the offender was plunged into water and pulled out again

explanation.surface: A penalty that had good times and bad.
explanation.walkthrough: A chair on a pivoting beam used to plunge scolds and suspected witches into a pond.
explanation.definitionFit: A seat on a pole for repeatedly lowering an offender into water as a public penalty.

clue.text: She is in the services associated with St. Mary-le-Bow

definitions.meaning: a member of the Women's Royal Naval Service
Christopher ... rebuilt this City of London church after the Great Fire

explanation.surface: A servicewoman with links to a famous London church.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the women's navy were nicknamed after its initials, and the architect Sir Christopher rebuilt the Bow Bells church.

clue.text: Babbling about fish and game? Poor soul

parts.note: a gar is a long-snouted fish
RU is rugby union

indicators.note: poor as in badly formed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone prattles on about fishing and hunting, the poor thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' rearranges SOUL into LOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Talkative to excess, chattering on without pause.

clue.text: Dumb actor is in walking-on part

definitions.meaning: a walk-on role has no lines, so its actor says nothing

explanation.surface: A foolish performer takes a small non-speaking role.
explanation.definitionFit: Lost for words, mute, like a walk-on extra who has no lines.

clue.text: Fittingly give support to king in cathedral city

parts.note: to prop is to support

indicators.note: in places the king inside the name of the cathedral city

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire
R is for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: It is right to back the monarch in a cathedral town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts R inside ELY, giving ERLY after PROP.
explanation.definitionFit: Done in a correct, suitable way, as is appropriate.

clue.text: He has, to get the balance right when tracing figures

definitions.text: He has, to get the balance right when tracing figures

parts.words: He has, to get the balance right when tracing figures
parts.note: the figures sound like sums in accounts, but they are the shapes cut on ice, where staying upright matters

explanation.surface: A bookkeeper must make the accounts balance when checking the numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Balance' and 'figures' suggest accounting; figures here are the patterns traced on ice.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone gliding on ice must keep balanced while carving figures.

clue.text: Gadarene progress involving 10 pets

indicators.note: involving in its sense of entangling, so the letters are twisted together

parts.note: the answer at 10, the honey drink

explanation.surface: A headlong rush that drags in drinks and animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' entangles MEAD (the answer at 10) with PETS. The Gadarene swine rushed down a slope into the sea in the Gospels.
explanation.definitionFit: A headlong panic rush, like the biblical swine that ran into the sea.

clue.text: Attention to your historic course, do we hear?

parts.note: ear means attention, as in 'lend an ear'
thy is the old form of your

explanation.surface: Someone is told to pay attention to their history lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'do we hear?' says the definition is a sound-alike: 'course' is heard as coarse, meaning crude.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthy humour is crude and vulgar, which is what coarse means.

clue.text: Veil raised in Brazilian city — an outstanding work of art

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the city's name

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the word is written upwards

explanation.surface: A veil is lifted at a Rio unveiling of a masterpiece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns VEIL into LIEV, which 'in' places inside RIO.
explanation.definitionFit: Relief sculpture in Italian; carved work stands out from its background.

clue.text: Phaeton's bizarre form of transport

indicators.note: something bizarre is twisted out of normal shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A strange mythical sun chariot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bizarre' rearranges PHAETONS. A phaeton is itself a light carriage, which lures the solver to think the clue is a definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A light open horse-drawn carriage named after a 19th-century clergyman.

clue.text: Several deliveries by spinner rise too high

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled
a top is a toy that spins

explanation.surface: A slow bowler's overs climb higher than intended.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an OVER is a series of six balls delivered by one bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: To surpass in height, to go above and beyond.

clue.text: Fashionable to complain about this sort of funny writing

indicators.note: about here means around, so the complaint wraps round the fashionable word

parts.note: to moan is to complain
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: It is trendy to grumble about comic writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Funny' means strange: Minoan Linear A script is still undeciphered.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bronze Age Cretans left a script, Linear A, that nobody can read.

clue.text: Girl beset by mishmash of national culture?

annotationWithheld.why: Girl beset by mishmash of national culture?: H(ELLEN)ISM needs 'mishmash' to supply the fodder MISH and also signal its rearrangement, one word doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Girl beset by mishmash of national culture?

clue.text: Ayesha would briefly identify this repository

parts.note: Ayesha is She, the immortal queen of Rider Haggard's novel
would shortened is 'd

explanation.surface: A woman named Ayesha would point out this store.
explanation.walkthrough: SHE'D, the short form of 'she would', with Ayesha standing for She.
explanation.definitionFit: A hut used to store tools or goods.

clue.text: Dreadful-sounding colourist

indicators.note: sounding means the word is said rather than spelt

parts.note: dreadful means dire

explanation.surface: A painter with an awful-sounding reputation.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who colours fabric with pigments.

clue.text: PM's private retreat in the East?

definitions.meaning: Anthony ... was British Prime Minister in 1955-57
the garden God planted eastward, in Genesis

explanation.surface: The Prime Minister's secluded hideaway somewhere in Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname of a postwar premier and the biblical garden paradise share a name.

clue.text: Remarkable memo to one of Fuller's characters

parts.note: a memo is a note
Thomas Fuller wrote The History of the Worthies of England, profiles of notable people

explanation.surface: An impressive note sent to a character created by Fuller.
explanation.definitionFit: Worth noticing, deserving attention.

clue.text: Berkshire village dispensing with a form of taxation

indicators.note: dispensing with means doing without, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: Ascot in Berkshire, home of the racecourse

explanation.surface: A Berkshire village abolishes a tax.
explanation.walkthrough: Ascot is a Berkshire village famous for its royal horse races.
explanation.definitionFit: Scot was a medieval levy, surviving in 'scot-free'.

clue.text: Damage to liner by uninvited visitor

indicators.note: damage wrecks things, so the letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: per means by, as in per post

explanation.surface: An intruder harms a cruise ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Damage' rearranges TOLINER into INTERLO, then PER follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who intrudes where they are not welcome.
